findings.description: The previous code used urlsplit, which handled bracketed IPv6 addresses such as '[::1]:5000' and also lowercased the hostname. partition(':') splits at the first colon, so sn_host becomes '[' and sn_port becomes ':1]:5000'. The int(sn_port) call then raises ValueError, or the host is wrong, whenever app.run() is used with an IPv6 SERVER_NAME.
findings.suggestion: Keep urlsplit(f'//{server_name}') for parsing, or use rpartition(':') with bracket handling.
findings.title: SERVER_NAME parsing with partition(':') breaks IPv6 literals

findings.description: The old code used urlsplit(host_url).hostname or 'localhost'. The new code uses request.host.partition(':')[0]. For an IPv6 Host header like '[::1]:5000' this yields '[', which is the wrong cookie domain, so cookies saved by session_transaction are not matched on later requests. An empty host also yields '' instead of 'localhost'. Hostname case is also no longer normalised.
findings.title: Cookie domain lost 'localhost' fallback and breaks IPv6 hosts
